macro.text: Wall Street closes sharply lower as AI cash-burn fears spark a tech selloff; Nasdaq down over 5% for its worst month since March 2025.
Fed officials, including Musalem, say they will need to get back to hiking rates.
Tankers defy a sharp escalation of Iranian attacks to keep crude flowing through the Strait of Hormuz.
Wage growth hits a 5-year low as take-home pay lags inflation.

bigNames.text: Fell in sympathy with Intel; MarketWatch says Intel's report revealed two big issues for AMD ahead of its Nov 3 report.
Worst day since the 1970s, wiping about $12B off the government's stake; analysts see no reason to buy the dip.
Reversed from -7% premarket: reclaimed 232.90 early and reached 241.55 at 11:25, just through the 241.24 gap edge, as chips kept falling.
All-time highs as refining profits soar on the Iran and Ukraine wars.

read: Tech risk-off held and deepened: SPY broke its opening range down at 10:15, low 750.36 at 2:50, closed -1.77%; QQQ -3.47%, SMH -7%. Puts sides held on INTC (63.20), RDDT (89.28), NVDA (200.92) and MU (861.59). AMZN went the other way, reclaiming 232.90 to 241.55; REGN broke 887 to 935. Money stayed in energy and staples. No red U.S. events Monday.
